title: A People's History of the United States
author: Howard Zinn
summary: Seminal revisionist history text presenting American history from the perspective of marginalized groups including Native Americans, African Americans, women, and working class. Challenges traditional nationalist narratives by emphasizing exploitation, resistance, and grassroots movements for social justice.

central_thesis.main_argument: America was built on the blood and suffering of the poor
central_thesis.historiographical_critique: Traditional history writing is never neutral but shaped by ideological choices that reinforce power structures
central_thesis.perspective_shift: History should emphasize experiences of ordinary people rather than elite figures

key_themes: Exploitation of lower classes by economic and political elites
Grassroots movements as drivers of social progress
Critique of 'national interest' as cover for corporate interests
Class conflict as underlying dynamic of American history
Resistance and agency of marginalized peoples

impact.educational_adoption: Widely assigned in high schools and colleges across US
impact.historiographical_influence: Changed focus of historical work to include previously ignored stories

connections: Critique of government-corporate nexus aligns with Sherlock research on intelligence community
Documentation of elite manipulation patterns applicable to understanding hidden power structures
Framework for analyzing how official narratives obscure uncomfortable truths
research_applications: Methodology for examining history from alternative perspectives
Framework for understanding grassroots resistance to institutional power

strengths: Challenges uncritical acceptance of official narratives
criticisms: Ideological bias affects credibility in some areas

research_quality: HIGH - Well-documented, influential text with extensive scholarly engagement
